narrative:
The model estimated a 47.0% probability that you would be a bad credit risk. That is not a certainty of default, but it was high enough to cross the bank’s acceptance line, so your application was denied.

The strongest factor increasing your risk was the purpose of the loan: a new car. This purpose is less common among approved applicants (about 16.5%) and pushed the decision toward bad credit. The next most important factor was the requested amount. At 6,260 DM, it is much higher than the approved average of about 3,020 DM, but in your case this factor worked in your favor, reducing rather than increasing the assessed risk. The third key factor was your checking-account status. A balance in the 0-200 DM range increased the risk; by comparison, most approved applicants had no balance recorded, and only a smaller share had this low-balance status.

To improve your next application, ask the bank to confirm which details mattered most. Consider requesting a smaller amount, strengthening your checking-account balance and savings record, and exploring whether adding a guarantor or co-applicant is possible. Reapplying only after those changes may give a clearer, stronger profile.
